pairs.description: Nagy 2008 and Nopens 2004 model evolving particle-size distributions in liquid systems, with Nagy 2008 describing paracetamol crystallization and Nopens 2004 describing activated-sludge flocculation. Both are dynamic population-balance models that predict particle-size distributions over time and are calibrated with particle-size measurements. Nagy 2008 covers primary nucleation and crystal growth and tracks four moments of the crystal-size distribution, using FBRM particle information and ATR-FTIR solution concentration; Nopens 2004 covers floc aggregation and breakage, solves size classes with the moving pivot method, and uses online laser-diffraction floc-size distributions.
